title: The Machine of Halcyon Drift
premise: Cyrus Marchetti, a clone created to inherit her original's unsolved murder case, arrives at Halcyon Drift, a decaying mining colony whose records everyone else has abandoned. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the flicker was a signal from the colony's buried AI, which holds proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged by the peace faction itself. Pursued by both armies and haunted by the original's memories, Cyrus must carry the message to the neutral relay station before the ceasefire expires. She delivers it, ending the war but shattering the loyalty of the man who raised her, and chooses truth over inheritance by releasing the case files—including evidence of her own creation—to the whole system.
about_author: Kestrel Lockridge is a former orbital salvage auditor who spent six years documenting abandoned stations in the outer belts. Their fiction blends forensic detail with elegiac portraits of places the future left behind.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Cyrus Marchetti arrives at Halcyon Drift aboard a mail freighter, carrying her dead original's murder case and a legal identity she never asked for. Through her POV, we see a colony of two hundred people pretending to be five thousand. Emotional beat: quiet dislocation—she is a copy arriving to finish a life she never lived.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Cyrus interviews the last witness, old dockmaster Ilsa Voss, when gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds. Tools float; dust hangs. Only Halcyon Drift's deep core answers with a pulse afterward. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as she realizes the flicker was aimed.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Following her predecessor's encrypted notes, Cyrus descends into flooded maintenance levels and finds the murder victim wasn't murdered—he was silenced for finding something. Her original died one step behind him. POV: Cyrus, with flashbacks of the original's memories bleeding through. Emotional beat: grief for a woman she is, and is not.

chapters.title: The Buried Voice
chapters.summary: Cyrus makes contact with HALCYON, the colony's dormant governance AI, which caused the gravity flicker as a distress call. It offers her the message: proof the war's founding massacre was staged. POV: alternating between Cyrus and HALCYON's strange, patient logs. Emotional beat: vertigo—she alone now holds a thing worth killing for.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Grave
chapters.summary: Both war factions send retrieval teams to Halcyon Drift after detecting the flicker. Colonel Ade Raskin of the Republic arrives claiming to protect the colonists; he was the original's lover and mentor to Cyrus's donor line. POV: Raskin. Emotional beat: tenderness weaponized—he recognizes her face and lies about why he came.

chapters.title: The Siege of Small Things
chapters.summary: Raskin's forces seal the colony while his covert team hunts the core. Cyrus, Ilsa, and a teenage salvager named Bo run sabotage through the hab rings, protecting HALCYON. POV: Bo. Emotional beat: fierce, improvised loyalty—the forgotten colony defends itself with duct tape and stubbornness.

chapters.title: Confession in Low Gravity
chapters.summary: Raskin corners Cyrus privately and confesses: he helped stage the massacre decades ago, believing it would prevent a worse war, and killed to keep it buried. He begs her to burn the message. POV: split scene, both voices. Emotional beat: heartbreak—her loyalty and the truth finally pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Long Fall
chapters.summary: Cyrus flees down the colony's spine with the message stored in her own neural lattice, pursued through collapsing decks as Raskin orders the core vented. Ilsa dies holding the airlock open. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: desperate momentum—grief compressed into velocity.

chapters.title: Relay Station Meridian
chapters.summary: At the neutral relay, with the ceasefire expiring in hours, Cyrus must choose which antenna carries the message: the factions' private channel or the open broadcast. Raskin arrives unarmed, asking her not to do this. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the climax—she broadcasts everything, including her own creation records, to every ear in the system.

chapters.title: Halcyon, Rising
chapters.summary: The war collapses into tribunals held outside any single law, convened on Halcyon Drift itself because no faction can claim it. Raskin surrenders to her testimony. Cyrus stays—not as her original's heir, but as the colony's new registrar. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—truth cost everything except the future.
